question: Assume today is 2026-08-19. You know nothing published after this date. Estimate the number of registered company insolvencies in England and Wales in August 2026 (the headline monthly total of compulsory liquidations, creditors' voluntary liquidations, administrations, company voluntary arrangements and receivership appointments, in which the first three are seasonally adjusted), as it will be first reported in the Insolvency Service's monthly Company Insolvency Statistics release.

target.what: Number of registered company insolvencies in England and Wales in August 2026, as the headline monthly total first reported by the Insolvency Service: compulsory liquidations, creditors' voluntary liquidations, administrations, company voluntary arrangements and receivership appointments, with the s
target.caveats: The target period is not complete at the 2026-08-19 cutoff and the first official report will be published after the cutoff. The first-reported value may be provisional and subject to later revision. The measure counts insolvency events for registered companies in England and Wales, not Companies Ho

candidates.hypothesis: The target is the next point in the same monthly series. The latest published July 2026 headline and component totals can be used as an anchor, multiplied by an August/July seasonal factor estimated from prior years, and adjusted for the recent year-on-year trend. Prior August observations and revisions constrain the plausible range.
candidates.data_to_find: Latest Insolvency Service monthly company insolvency statistics release and data tables available before 2026-08-19, ideally for July 2026: headline total, compulsory liquidations, CVLs, administrations, CVAs and receiverships; whether each series is seasonally adjusted; August and July values for as many prior years as available, at least 2023-2025; revision history. Minimum evidence: July 2026 headline plus three historical August/July ratios and recent year-on-year change.

candidates.hypothesis: The headline total equals the sum of five case types. The dominant CVL series and the smaller compulsory liquidation and administration series can be forecast separately using recent levels, August seasonality and component-specific seasonal factors; summing the component forecasts gives the target and reveals composition risk.
candidates.data_to_find: Monthly England and Wales counts by case type for January-July 2026 and prior August values for 2023-2025; published seasonally adjusted and non-seasonally adjusted series; any component-specific seasonal factors; the CVL share of the headline and any coverage breaks. Minimum evidence: recent component levels and August component ratios.

candidates.hypothesis: Monthly insolvencies can be estimated as active registered company stock multiplied by a monthly insolvency rate. The stock is slow-moving and observable; the monthly rate has seasonal and cyclical patterns. Applying a defensible August rate to mid-2026 active company stock gives an independent estimate.

Minimum evidence: active company stock and a defensible August monthly insolvency rate.

candidates.hypothesis: Insolvency notices published in the Gazette are an administrative trace of liquidations, administrations, CVAs and receiverships. Counts in August 2026, observed through 2026-08-19 plus an expected remainder, should move with the official total, though notice duplication, timing lag and type coverage require a bridge factor estimated from prior months.
candidates.data_to_find: London Gazette insolvency notices for August 2026 by notice type, including winding-up petitions or orders, creditor meetings, liquidator or administrator appointments, CVAs and receiverships; comparable August 2023-2025 counts; mapping to Insolvency Service case types; publication lag. Minimum evidence: partial August notice counts and a historical August notice-to-official-count ratio.

candidates.hypothesis: Compulsory liquidations are driven by winding-up petitions and orders; CVLs follow creditor meetings and resolutions. Court petitions or orders and Companies House liquidation filings in August 2026 are leading or coincident administrative indicators. Historical conversion ratios translate them into case counts, with lags and coverage adjustments.

Minimum evidence: partial August petition or order count and a historical petition-to-liquidation ratio.

Forecasts provide an outside constraint if they are independent of the Insolvency Service headline.

Minimum evidence: one credible 2026 annual forecast and an August annual-share range.

candidates.hypothesis: Monthly insolvency counts respond to interest rates, inflation, GDP, unemployment and corporate distress indices. As of August 2026, current macro readings can shift the baseline from a pure seasonal extrapolation; historical elasticities or distressed-company shares provide the bridge. The direction depends on whether conditions are tighter or looser than the recent baseline.
candidates.data_to_find: Latest pre-cutoff UK macro readings, including Bank Rate, CPI, GDP, unemployment and insolvency-related distress indices, for August 2026; historical monthly relationship between these indicators and England and Wales company insolvency counts. Minimum evidence: current macro surprise versus 2025 and a plausible elasticity or qualitative direction.

assessment.note: Latest Insolvency Service headline levels (Nov 2025-Jun 2026) show a 2026 run-rate around 1.7k-2.1k, with May and June near 1.85k. p77/p78 are revised upward from older p90/p89; p74 is an older April 2026 vintage and p26's quoted July-release row implies a slight downward revision. Shared source and revision risk.
Historical anchors: Aug 2025 2048, Jul 2025 2083, Aug 2024 1933, Jun 2025 2048, Apr 2025 2028, Feb 2025 2015. Support a prior-year August level near 2.0k and a modest year-on-year decline into 2026.
August 2025 components sum exactly to p1 2048: compulsory 311, CVL 1600, administration 121, CVA 16, receivership 0. Confirms CVL dominance and negligible receiverships.

2026 component rows: June components sum to p14 1845; May components sum to p15 1849; April p26 row plus p27 components sum to about 2079, while older p74 total is 2085. Administrations are elevated versus August 2025, and revisions exist.

England and Wales 12-month insolvency rates around 51-55 per 10,000, declining slightly; p116 gives the reciprocal one in 194. Supports a monthly flow near 2k, though the rate is an annual-average measure.

UK company register is growing; effective register was 4.93m at end March 2026. E&W quarterly change 27,233 versus Scotland 1,804 and NI -356 shows E&W dominates the UK register. Needed to convert UK effective register to E&W with an explicit share assumption.
August 2025 was about 2% below July and 6% above August 2024; CVL shares were 74-78% across months. p9 is rounded: p1/p2 is about -1.7%, not exactly -2%.

HMRC share of High Court winding-up petitions fell from over 80% in early 2026 to 62% in a five-week period. Periods differ, so this is not a direct aggregate contradiction but indicates a shift in enforcement mix.
Month-to-month volatility is 9-11%; the recent four-month average 1,789 is below the 2022-25 average 1,982, consistent with lower 2026 levels and wide monthly uncertainty.
Real-estate connected administrations (~200 in March-April, 73 in April) explain elevated 2026 administration counts and are relevant to component forecast risk.

Seasonal adjustment can move monthly numbers by up to 10%; April compulsory liquidations get a 20-30% Easter adjustment. The April-specific factor is not applicable to August, but it supports using the seasonally adjusted series.

April 2026 total: p74 says 2,085 in the May release, while p26's quoted July-release row lists 2,079 (p26's value field is compulsory liquidations 384). Indicates a revision; latest vintage should be preferred where available.

The series is irregular, so the fallback should anchor on August 2025 p1 and the latest June 2026 year-on-year movement from p14/p16; the other months supply level and seasonal context. assumptions.rationale: p29 gives the UK effective register 4,930,634 at end March 2026, while p31/p33/p34 show E&W quarterly register growth of 27,233 versus Scotland 1,804 and NI -356. E&W therefore dominates the UK register; Companies House register composition is historically around 93-94% E&W. This share is needed only to convert p29's UK scope to E&W.

assumptions.falsified_by: A published E&W effective register or E&W share outside roughly 90-96% of the UK effective register.

assumptions.rationale: p116 is a 12-month ending February 2026 measure. p87 shows the 12-month rate to April 2026 at 51.8 versus p113's 51.5 to February, only about +0.6%. Month-to-month insolvency changes average 9-11% (p84), and August seasonal effects are modest compared with that. A central factor near 1.0 with a wide range is appropriate.
assumptions.applies_when: Using the 12-month ending February 2026 rate p116 to estimate the August 2026 monthly flow.
assumptions.falsified_by: Evidence of a large August 2026 seasonal shift or a material change in the E&W insolvency rate after April 2026.

assumptions.rationale: The June 2026 headline is about 10% below June 2025 (p14/p16). Recent compulsory liquidation counts p17 June 276, p22 May 281 and p26 April 384 are below the August 2025 level p4 311, so a 0.9 factor is central, with a wide range for court/petition timing.
assumptions.applies_when: Scaling p4 August 2025 compulsory liquidations to August 2026 in the component-sum route.
assumptions.falsified_by: New winding-up petition or order data showing compulsory liquidations rising materially above or falling well below the recent trend.

assumptions.name: Year-on-year factor for CVLs, August 2026 versus August 2025
assumptions.rationale: The total June 2026 year-on-year decline is about 10% (p14/p16). June 2026 CVLs p18 1,364 are below August 2025 p5 1,600, and recent CVL counts have softened. A factor near 0.9 is central, with a narrower range than the more volatile components.
assumptions.applies_when: Scaling p5 August 2025 CVLs to August 2026 in the component-sum route.
assumptions.falsified_by: Creditor-meeting or Companies House liquidation filing data showing CVLs materially different from the recent decline trend.

methods.rationale: Own-history forecast of the monthly headline target. The list uses first-reported or contemporaneous target values: recent months p93/p92/p77/p78/p75/p74/p15/p14, plus year-earlier anchors p1/p2/p16/p76/p91/p3. assumptions.name: England and Wales share of UK effective register
assumptions.rationale: p29 is a UK effective-register denominator while the target is E&W only. E&W dominates the UK register; p31/p33/p34 give recent E&W, Scotland and Northern Ireland register movements but no E&W effective-register level. The share is placed near the high end because E&W is much larger than the other UK jurisdictions.
assumptions.applies_when: Used to convert the UK effective-register denominator in p29 to an E&W-equivalent denominator for the rate route.
assumptions.falsified_by: An E&W effective-register share outside the stated range, or a published E&W effective-register level materially different from this share of p29.

assumptions.name: August 2026 monthly rate adjustment versus 12-month average ending February 2026
assumptions.rationale: p116 gives the E&W 12-month rate to February 2026. p113, p87 and p12 show a generally declining 12-month rate into 2026, and recent monthly levels p14/p15 are below the year-earlier p16 comparison. August 2026 is therefore expected slightly below the 12-month average rate, with a wide range because the target month is incomplete and seasonally adjusted.
assumptions.applies_when: Used to convert the 12-month average rate embedded in p116 into an August 2026 monthly-rate factor.
assumptions.falsified_by: Evidence that August 2026 insolvency activity rebounded to or above the 12-month average ending February 2026.

assumptions.name: Year-on-year factor for compulsory liquidations, August 2026 versus August 2025
assumptions.rationale: p4 is the August 2025 compulsory-liquidation anchor. Recent 2026 compulsory levels p17 and p22 are below p4, while p26 includes an April spike. Winding-up activity indicators p128, p129, p138 and p124 point to elevated petitions/orders, but p58/p59 show the HMRC petition share falling. The factor is centred near flat with a wide range.
assumptions.applies_when: Applied to p4 to project August 2026 compulsory liquidations.
assumptions.falsified_by: A clear August 2026 petition/order collapse or a sustained compulsory-liquidation level far outside the recent p17/p22/p26 range.

assumptions.name: Year-on-year factor for CVLs, August 2026 versus August 2025
assumptions.rationale: p5 is the August 2025 CVL anchor. Recent 2026 CVL levels p18 and p23 are lower, and p117 indicates Q1 2026 CVLs were only slightly below Q1 2025. p135 is a gross May Gazette CVL-resolutions count and needs caution. The factor allows for a modest decline, not a repeat of the full headline year-on-year fall.
assumptions.applies_when: Applied to p5 to project August 2026 CVLs.
assumptions.falsified_by: Sustained CVL resolutions at or above the 2025 level through summer 2026, or a sharper collapse than the stated range.

assumptions.name: Year-on-year factor for administrations, August 2026 versus August 2025
assumptions.rationale: p6 is the August 2025 administration anchor. Recent administration counts p19, p24, p27 and p110 are generally higher than p6. p121 indicates a Q1 2026 increase even excluding connected appointments, while p85/p86/p119 show a temporary connected real-estate administration blip. The factor is above one but not as high as the raw connected-appointment spike.
assumptions.applies_when: Applied to p6 to project August 2026 administrations.
assumptions.falsified_by: Evidence that the connected-administration effect fully unwinds and August 2026 administrations return to near the p6 level or below.

assumptions.name: Year-on-year factor for CVAs, August 2026 versus August 2025
assumptions.rationale: p7 is the August 2025 CVA anchor. Recent CVA counts p20, p25, p82 and p111 are volatile and show no clear trend. A flat central factor with a wide range reflects that volatility and the small count size.
assumptions.applies_when: Applied to p7 to project August 2026 CVAs.
assumptions.falsified_by: A sustained run of CVA counts well above or below the 2025 and early-2026 range.

The best estimate for registered company insolvencies in England and Wales in August 2026 (headline monthly total, seasonally adjusted) is 1,879 insolvency (80% model-based interval 1,293 to 2,730 insolvency).

Evidence: an own-history year-on-year route (1,963) and a June-to-August seasonal bridge (1,844) use observed months including 1,845 registered company insolvencies, 2,048 registered company insolvencies and 2,048 registered company insolvencies. A component-sum route (1,915) scales August 2025 components 311 compulsory liquidations, 1,600 creditors' voluntary liquidations, 121 administrations and 16 company voluntary arrangements by assumed factors 0.95 to 1. A rate route (1,825) divides the effective register 4,930,634 companies by 194 companies on effective register per insolvency, adjusted by assumptions 0.935 and 0.93.

Code combined four overlapping-evidence blocks with equal weight per block, taking the median; the interval reflects the blocks' own widths.
